C-FEATURE-TRANSACTIONAL-ACTIVATION-SLICE.Summary: Prove the Worldline product hypothesis with one useful AI-generated browser feature that follows generate, validate, test, permission review, stage, activate, monitor, quarantine, and rollback through the real feature host, browser gateway, trusted UI, and durable package generation.
C-FEATURE-TRANSACTIONAL-ACTIVATION-SLICE.Problem: The platform has many isolated models and proving fixtures but no single user or AI-generated feature traverses the complete security and recovery architecture. Without a transactional end-to-end slice, individual green subsystems can still compose into an unsafe activation path, hidden authority escalation, unrecoverable update, or browser-wide failure.

Goals.Goal: Generate one bounded feature candidate in an isolated builder from a human-readable feature request.
Validate source, manifest, imports, capabilities, limits, provenance, and compatibility before any activation authority exists.
Run deterministic contract, malicious-input, and failure tests against a disposable profile.
Show a trusted permission diff and require explicit activation authorization distinct from code generation and package installation.
Activate one immutable generation atomically, monitor it, and recover from crash, loop, denial, incompatible update, and bad revision.
Demonstrate useful page observation, bounded UI composition, and a separately authorized browser action on real CEF.

Constraints.Constraint: SPEC APPROVAL DOES NOT APPROVE A PLAN OR IMPLEMENTATION.
All preceding vNext packages in the package index must be applied before this change is planned.
The AI builder has no installation, runtime, browser profile, credentials, network, activation, grant, updater, or recovery authority.
Generated source, package installation, permission grant, and activation are separate recorded operations.
The proving feature runs as an ordinary untrusted WASM feature and receives no test-only privilege or native escape hatch.
All browser and I/O effects use the same production brokers and real CEF path used outside the test.
Automatic rollback may restore local code, state, policy, and UI composition but cannot claim to undo external effects already dispatched.
Reference fixtures supplement but cannot replace the required real desktop and fresh-process evidence.
Failure of the feature cannot prevent trusted stop, disable, quarantine, normal browsing, updater, or recovery boot.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Proving all future generated features safe or correct.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: A fixed feature request produces source and an immutable package candidate inside a disposable build sandbox with recorded toolchain and input provenance.
Static and dynamic validation rejects forbidden imports, undeclared capabilities, native artifacts, path escape, unbounded views, unsupported engine profiles, and incompatible ABI or state schemas.
The candidate passes deterministic tests against a disposable installation and cannot access the active user profile, credentials, arbitrary network, filesystem, or process APIs.
Trusted UI shows exact added and removed capabilities, resources, duration, engine requirements, and data-access implications before activation.
Installation does not activate the feature; an explicit activation operation atomically selects one code, state, policy, authority, and UI generation.

The feature observes a real CEF page through bounded semantic query, renders a declarative sidebar summary, and performs one separately authorized typed navigation or page action without raw script access.

Fault injection at generate, build, validate, test, migration, select, start, observe, and promote leaves either the prior generation current or the candidate quarantined with protected recovery available.
Revocation or stop during an in-flight action prevents any later privileged commit through the effect fence.
Trap, loop, memory growth, host-call flood, invalid UI model, and backend crash remain confined and do not terminate normal browsing or recovery.
An incompatible core or engine profile update disables the optional feature while preserving its package and data and leaves trusted browsing available.
Monitoring records activation epoch, capability use counts, denials, resource limits, health, rollback reason, and causality without raw page content or secrets.
The completion packet labels contract, reference, real CEF, OS isolation, fresh-process, UI accessibility, local, and hosted evidence separately.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: One ordinary generated feature completes the full transaction on real CEF and trusted UI while fault injection, revocation, resource abuse, incompatible update, quarantine, and fresh-process recovery preserve the trusted browser baseline.

Assumptions.Assumption: A page-outline sidebar with one separately authorized typed action is useful enough to test the hypothesis without adding model-provider or external-service dependencies.
Every required prior package exposes a stable enough contract for one end-to-end proving feature.
Hosted OS, CEF, and UI evidence can be separated into required platform jobs without making live public services part of CI.
